result.area_summary: The graph crate's transport is in good shape: one retrying core with verb-derived RetryClass, body serialized once, CAE single re-mint, same-origin guard on every nextLink follow, inner-429 re-batching under the shared RetryBudget, and tenant-prefixed self-invalidating caches — all heavily documented and mostly pinned by wiremock tests. The weak spots are at the seams: `list_all_sites` is the one capped tenant-wide scan that drops its truncation flag (so a >5000-site tenant's sweep is cached as complete), the grant read-through cache sits on the per-SP `appRoleAssignments` read while the tenant-wide `appRoleAssignedTo` read it describes stays uncached, the SharePoint resolver collapses 403/429/401 into "did not resolve", and the advanced-query flag is inconsistent between page 1 and continuations. Several of the most recently fixed transport behaviours (non-idempotent POST not replayed, scoped bearer on batch page 2, CAE once-only guard) have no regression test.

findings.title: list_all_sites drops its truncation signal, so a >5000-site tenant's Sites.Selected sweep is reported and cached as complete
findings.rationale: Every other capped tenant-wide scan in this crate (`list_applications_all`, `list_saml_sso_service_principals`, `collect_all_pages_capped`) returns `(rows, truncated)` precisely so a caller cannot present a partial view as complete. `list_all_sites` is the exception: it silently truncates to `max` and returns a bare Vec. The sweep therefore has no way to know it stopped at site 5000; it sets `total_sites = sites.len()`, `is_complete()` returns true, the result is cached for the audit TTL, and `AppSiteAccessDto::from_sweep` reads an empty match list as 'no per-site grants'. On a tenant with more than 5000 sites, an app's Sites.Selected grants on any site past the cap are invisible and the panel affirmatively says the app has none — the exact 'coverage is never overstated' invariant the surrounding code and sharepoint-selected.md promise. There is no `total_sites >= MAX_SITES_PER_SWEEP` check anywhere in the command or the frontend (grep of web-rs for MAX_SITES/5000 finds nothing).
findings.proposal: Change `list_all_sites` to return `Result<(Vec<Site>, bool)>` where the bool is `page.next_link.is_some() || pages hit MAX_PAGES` when the cap stops the walk (mirror `collect_all_pages_capped`'s tail logic, or add a scoped `collect_pages_from_capped` helper and reuse it here). In `sweep_site_permissions` bind the flag, add `truncated: bool` to `SiteSweepResult`/`AppSiteAccessDto` (additive field), fold it into `is_complete()` (`!cancelled && sites_failed == 0 && !truncated`), skip caching when truncated, and render the existing `IndexCapNotice` pattern in the Sites tab. Add a wiremock test where page 1 already exceeds `max` and assert `truncated == true`.

findings.title: Grant read-through cache is attached to the per-SP appRoleAssignments read; the tenant-wide appRoleAssignedTo read it describes is uncached
findings.rationale: The comment, the cache-key name (`assigned_to:`) and the stated motivation (audit + consent lens paying for the same full-tenant scan twice) all describe `appRoleAssignedTo` on the Microsoft Graph SP — but both real callers (`prefetch_graph_app_roles` in audit.rs:957 and the consent scan in consent.rs:197) call `list_app_role_assigned_to`, which has no cache. `appRoleAssignments` (what one SP holds) is a small per-SP list that is cheap to re-read; caching it instead brings a 60-minute staleness window to the pre-write `existing` reads in permissions.rs:666 / sharepoint.rs:307 for no measurable win. The only test that touches the key (`deleting_a_service_principal_drops_the_grant_matrices`) seeds `grants:assigned_to:sp-1` by hand, so nothing proves which method writes it. caching-and-search.md ('Page size is a wall-clock divisor') names this read as the one that dominates the audit and consent view, so the intended win is currently not realized.
findings.proposal: Move the read-through block to `list_app_role_assigned_to` (key `grants:assigned_to:{sp}`), and either drop the cache from `list_app_role_assignments` or re-key it `grants:assignments:{sp}`; both mutator families already sweep the `grants:` prefix on Ok so invalidation is unchanged. Fix the doc comments to match. Add a wiremock test with `.expect(1)` on `/servicePrincipals/sp-graph/appRoleAssignedTo` called twice, and assert the existing `a_grant_write_invalidates_the_cached_matrices` shape for it.

findings.title: SharePoint resolver reports 403/429/401 on the subsite probe as 'did not resolve to a list, library or item'
findings.rationale: Only a 404 means 'not a subsite'. `get_site_by_url` rides `scoped_get_retried`, so after the retry budget a 429 still surfaces as `Throttled`; a user who lacks rights on the subsite gets `Forbidden`; an expired token gets `Unauthorized`. All three are collapsed into a `Protocol` error whose text tells the operator the URL is wrong. Downstream, `sharepoint_item_err` -> `map_sharepoint_err` only splices the capability catalog's remediation when `ui.code == "forbidden"` (graph_err.rs:26), so the 403 remediation for `sharepoint_selected_items` is bypassed too, and `retryable` is false for what was a throttle. In the multi-target grant loop (commands/sharepoint.rs:567) this becomes a warning 'could not resolve <url>' that misdirects the operator to fix the URL.
findings.proposal: Match `Err(GraphError::NotFound(_))` for the 'not a subsite' branch and `Err(e) => return Err(e)` for everything else. Add a wiremock test: site lookup returns 403 on the descent URL and the resolver must return `Forbidden`, not `Protocol`.

findings.title: Scoped writes (group membership, site/list/item grants, claims policies) bypass the retry loop entirely, so a 429 with Retry-After fails immediately where the identical unscoped write would be replayed
findings.rationale: The 'one-shot configuration write' rationale no longer holds: `add_group_member` is called from the DR restore loop over every restored SP, and `grant_list_permission`/`grant_list_item_permission`/`grant_site_permission` run inside the multi-target grant loop. `RetryReason::Throttled` is explicitly documented in http_retry.rs as safe to replay for any verb ('the service rejected the request before doing any work'), and `send_core_url_with` already takes an explicit provider plus `RetryClass::NonIdempotent` — the scoped GET family (`scoped_get_retried`) already made this move. Today a write that rides `write_token` gets its 429 honored exactly per Retry-After; the same PATCH/POST on `sharepoint_token` or `group_member_token` fails on the first 429 and the restore/grant loop records a failure the operator has to redo. AGENTS.md's 'one definition per policy' rule for the retry budget is what this violates.
findings.proposal: Reimplement `scoped_send_core` as `self.send_core_url_with(token, RetryClass::NonIdempotent, method, url, &[], false, body_value, None)` — throttles replayed with Retry-After, transients not (so no double-commit risk), and the throttle observer sees the 429s so `ConcurrencyThrottle` can back the loops off. Keep `scoped_get` one-shot if the feature probes still want to degrade fast. Add a wiremock test: scoped POST 429 (Retry-After: 0) then 201 succeeds; scoped POST 502 is not replayed (`.expect(1)`).

findings.title: Advanced-query flag is inconsistent between page 1 and continuations: collect_all_pages defaults to eventual, the SP index does the reverse
findings.rationale: Of the 12 `collect_all_pages` callers, only two (`list_service_principal_groups`, `list_tenant_app_role_resources`) issue page 1 with `ConsistencyLevel: eventual`; the other ten (owners, oauth2 grants, appRoleAssignedTo, federated credentials, managed identities, application templates, batch overflow continuations) issue page 1 without the header and every later page with it, so a multi-page collection is served half from the primary store and half from the eventually-consistent index. The SP index inverts it: `$count=true` + eventual on page 1, plain on pages 2+; per Microsoft's advanced-query doc the `$count=true` that rides the nextLink is then 'silently ignored', and `total_count` has no reader here anyway (the comment's justification — 'keeps the response shape identical to the prior index calls' — is not a functional reason; `list_application_index_named` already dropped `$count` for exactly the reasons applications.rs:244-249 lists). The transport's own history (transport.rs:307-316) shows page-1/page-2 header drift producing a silent wrong answer once already.
findings.proposal: Delete the defaulted `collect_all_pages` wrapper (or default it to `false`) and make every call site pass the same flag it used for page 1 — mechanical, ten sites become `collect_all_pages_with(page, false)` and two become `true`. Drop `$count=true`/eventual from `list_service_principals_index` so page 1 matches its continuation (or, if there is a reason the index must be an advanced query, pass `true` to `collect_all_pages_capped` and document it). Add a wiremock regression for the transport.rs:307 bug: `list_applications_all` with `$expand` must have `header_is_missing("consistencylevel")` on the `page=2` mock — no test currently asserts that.

findings.title: Inner $batch 5xx sub-responses are terminal while the same GET alone would be retried
findings.rationale: The single-request transport retries every 5xx (transport.rs:613-651: anything not 4xx falls to `Attempt::Retry`), but inside a batch a 502/503/504 on one sub-request is mapped straight to `Server` and never re-batched. So the same object read has two retry policies depending on whether it travelled batched or alone — for the DR backup that means a transient 503 on one sub-request becomes a permanently 'skipped' object in the backup manifest, and for the audit prewarm a cold lean-SP entry. Microsoft's throttling guidance for batching says to retry each failed request from the batch individually; the machinery (`pending`/`throttled` index list + `RetryBudget`) is already there for 429.
findings.proposal: Extend the re-batch predicate to `matches!(sub.status, 429 | 502 | 503 | 504) && budget.may_retry()`, keeping the observer notification for 429 only, and let `budget.wait(max_retry_after)` fall back to jittered backoff when no inner Retry-After exists. Add a wiremock test mirroring `batch_get_json_retries_inner_429_then_surfaces_throttled` with an inner 503 that succeeds on the second POST.

findings.title: No graph-level regression test that a non-idempotent POST is NOT replayed after a 502 / connection reset (the addPassword double-mint bug)
findings.rationale: Commit 8fb1ac7 fixed `POST .../addPassword` being replayed up to three times after a 502, minting orphaned client secrets the operator never saw. The policy now lives in `core::http_retry::with_retries` (unit-tested there), but the graph-side mapping that decides the class — `retry_class_for` plus the explicit `RetryClass::Idempotent` override on the `$batch` POST — has no test in this crate. A future edit that routes a POST through `send_core_url_with(.., RetryClass::Idempotent, ..)` or changes `retry_class_for` would pass the whole suite. The module header claims 'the behavioral contracts (retry budget, CAE single re-mint, origin guard, ...) are unchanged and pinned by tests/transport.rs' — the retry-class contract is not.
findings.proposal: Add three wiremock tests in tests/transport.rs: (1) `add_password` against a 502 mock with `.expect(1)` returns `Err(GraphError::Server{..})` and is not re-sent; (2) `get_organization` 502-then-200 succeeds (Idempotent replays); (3) `batch_get_json` 502-then-200 on `/$batch` succeeds (explicit Idempotent override). Also pin the CAE once-only guard: a provider whose `bearer_with_claims` returns a token that is still challenged must yield `Unauthorized` after exactly two requests.

findings.title: Zero wiremock coverage for the scoped batch continuation, the SP signing-cert password sweep, the Prefer-header gallery fetch and several other client methods
findings.rationale: Each of these encodes a non-obvious contract that was learned the hard way and is documented in a block comment: the scoped bearer must ride page 2 of a batched site read (a real 403 bug), `remove_service_principal_key_credential` must drop the paired `passwordCredentials` entry by `customKeyIdentifier` or strand a PFX password forever, `list_all_application_templates` must send `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=2800` on the first request only, `get_application_backup_json` must `$select` the exact `APP_BACKUP_SELECT` projection and `$expand=owners` without the advanced-query header, `patch_application_expose_api`/`set_application_app_roles` must sweep the `resource:` prefix (only the SP-side twin is tested), and a `$batch` envelope missing an id must yield `Protocol`. None has a test, so each can regress silently.
findings.proposal: Add one focused wiremock test per contract in the matching tests/*.rs module: (a) `batch_list_site_permissions` whose sub-response carries a nextLink and a `page=2` mock that requires `Authorization: Bearer sp`; (b) `remove_service_principal_key_credential` with a Sign/Verify pair plus a passwordCredential sharing the thumbprint, asserting the PATCH body drops all three and keeps unrelated entries; (c) `list_all_application_templates` with `header("prefer", "odata.maxpagesize=2800")` on page 1 and `header_is_missing("prefer")` on page 2; (d) backup JSON `$select`/`$expand` + `header_is_missing("consistencylevel")`; (e) `patch_application_expose_api` clears a seeded `tenant-test|resource:...` key; (f) batch envelope with a missing id -> `Protocol`.

findings.title: Two hand-rolled nextLink loops duplicate collect_pages_from (same_origin + MAX_PAGES + append)
findings.rationale: `collect_pages_from` exists precisely to be the one origin-guarded, page-bounded follower for scoped reads (`list_conditional_access_policies`, `list_site_permissions`, `list_site_drives`, ... all use it). The sign-in-activity report and the site enumeration re-implement it inline, so the origin guard and the page cap are maintained in three places; `list_all_sites` additionally needs the capped/truncated shape (finding 1). Five copies of `MAX_PAGES` can drift.
findings.proposal: Route `list_service_principal_sign_in_activities` through `collect_pages_from(first, |u| self.scoped_get(token, &u))` (it already uses `scoped_get` per page, so behaviour is unchanged). Add `collect_pages_from_capped(first, max, fetch) -> Result<(Vec<T>, bool)>` next to it and use it for `list_all_sites`, which also delivers finding 1's truncation flag. Hoist `MAX_PAGES` to a single `pub(crate) const` in transport.rs.

findings.title: Five copies of the 'GET single object, 404 -> Ok(None)' match; two raw-JSON app readers differ only in $select
findings.rationale: The 404-to-None mapping is the crate's convention for 'object vanished between index read and detail read', and it is restated verbatim in five methods (the batched variant `batch_get_service_principals` has a sixth spelling). A single `get_json_optional<T>(path, query)` in transport.rs would make the convention one line per caller and make a future change (e.g. also treating a specific 400 `Request_ResourceNotFound` body as None) a one-place edit.
findings.proposal: Add `pub(crate) async fn get_json_optional<T: DeserializeOwned>(&self, path: &str, query: &[(&str,&str)]) -> Result<Option<T>>` to transport.rs and collapse the five call sites; optionally fold `get_application_sso_fields`/`get_application_auth_fields` into `get_application_fields_raw(object_id, select)` with two thin public wrappers so callers and tests are untouched.

findings.title: list_conditional_access_policies pages without $top, contrary to the 'every paged read sends $top' invariant
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md states 'Every paged read sends `$top` (`client::MAX_PAGE_SIZE`)' and caching-and-search.md explains why (serial paging, default page of 100). This read follows nextLink to exhaustion but sends no `$top`; Microsoft's 'List policies' reference lists `$top` among the supported parameters for `/identity/conditionalAccess/policies`. Most tenants have well under 100 CA policies so the cost is usually one round trip, but large/MSP tenants do exceed it and the read rides the one-shot `scoped_get` that does not retry, so each extra page is another unretried chance to fail the whole tab.
findings.proposal: Build the URL with `?$top={MAX_PAGE_SIZE}` (Graph clamps an over-ask silently, matching the crate's stated rule), and extend `conditional_access_policies_parse_and_follow_paging` to match `query_param("$top", "999")` on page 1.

findings.title: upsert_admin_oauth2_grant_in fabricates a Graph 500 for a client-side invariant instead of using Protocol
findings.rationale: `GraphError::Protocol` exists for exactly this ('Client-side contract violation', http_error.rs). Reporting a synthetic `Api { status: 500 }` surfaces as ui_code `graph_error` and reads in logs and the UI as though Graph returned a server error, sending an operator (or a support engineer reading the trace) after a Graph outage that never happened.
findings.proposal: Replace with `GraphError::Protocol("existing oauth2PermissionGrant has no id".into())`; no caller matches on `Api{status:500}` for this path.

findings.title: remove_key_credential / remove_service_principal_key_credential PATCH the unchanged array and report success when the key id is not present
findings.rationale: Both fetch-modify-PATCH removers write the full collection back even when nothing matched `key_id` (another admin already removed it, or the audit's cached finding is stale). The write is a no-op on Graph but the caller sees `Ok(())`, so the audit's one-click 'remove expired credentials' Fix and bulk remove report a removal that did not happen, and the command layer then busts `apps_pairing`/detail/audit caches for nothing. `remove_password` (the `removePassword` action) gets a real 404 from Graph in the same situation, so the two credential kinds behave differently.
findings.proposal: Compare lengths before and after the filter (or `find` the entry first) and return `Err(GraphError::NotFound(format!("keyCredential {key_id}")))` when nothing was removed, skipping the PATCH. Callers already map NotFound for the password path; the audit remediation's 'already gone' handling then stays honest. Add a wiremock test asserting no PATCH is sent for an unknown key id.

findings.title: Crate-level docs misstate the retry set and claim ConsistencyLevel is added automatically
findings.rationale: This is the first thing a contributor (or an agent) reads about the transport. It undersells the retry set (any 5xx, plus the RetryClass split introduced in 8fb1ac7 is not mentioned at all), overstates jitter (an explicit Retry-After is honored verbatim per http_retry.rs), and the 'automatically' claim would lead someone to omit the `eventual` flag on a new `$count` query and get a silently-ignored `$count` (per Microsoft's advanced-query doc).
findings.proposal: Rewrite the two bullets: 'Retries 429 (Retry-After honored exactly), any 5xx and network errors under `core::http_retry`; POST/PATCH are replayed only after a 429 (`RetryClass`)'; 'Callers opt into advanced queries per request via the `consistency_eventual` flag — the header is never inferred from the query string.'

result.coverage_notes: Read fully: Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/error.rs, src/client.rs, client/{applications,batch,credentials,directory,policies,roles_grants,service_principals,sharepoint,transport}.rs and every file under client/tests/. Cross-checked against core http_retry.rs, http_error.rs, net.rs, token.rs (BearerProvider), models.rs (Paged/OAuth2PermissionGrant/SitePermission/SelectedPermission), dto sharepoint.rs, and the src-tauri callers named in the findings (audit.rs, consent.rs, sharepoint.rs, backup.rs, restore.rs, graph_err.rs, dispatch.rs, sso/mod.rs, enterprise_application.rs). Did not run cargo (per instructions). Three Graph facts verified via Microsoft Learn (CA policies list supports $top; servicePrincipalSignInActivities remains beta-only; $count=true without ConsistencyLevel is silently ignored). Did not independently test live Graph behaviour for mixed-consistency paging (finding on advanced-query flag is about inconsistency and the code's own stated rule, not an observed failure).

result.area_summary: The pure-decision half of the crate (targets.rs, verdict.rs, aap.rs, references.rs) is in excellent shape: fail-closed by construction, every past regression pinned by a named test, and the OPATH MemberOfGroup parser handles escaping, lookalike properties, blank operands and non-ASCII correctly. The weak half is the transport and error plumbing: send_core open-codes the retry loop against core::http_retry primitives instead of with_retries, so it never adopted RetryClass and still replays New-/Remove- cmdlets after a 5xx or connection reset (the exact defect commit 8fb1ac7 fixed for Graph/ARM/Key Vault), mid-pagination errors are flattened to Protocol (losing re-auth-fatal classification), and ExchangeError sits outside core::http_error_enum! despite AGENTS.md saying the taxonomy comes from it. A few consistency gaps remain between the crate's case-folded post-write proof and unfolded DN comparisons in its callers, two list-all reads feeding the irreversible group-delete gate use invoke_optional, and docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md still names value-only functions that a repo invariant pins as deleted.

findings.title: Exchange transport replays non-idempotent cmdlets (New-/Remove-) on 5xx and network errors
findings.rationale: Commit 8fb1ac7 ("stop replaying writes") added RetryReason/RetryClass to with_retries so a POST that hit a connection reset or 502 after the server committed is not replayed; Graph, ARM and Key Vault all route through with_retries + retry_class_for. The Exchange transport never used with_retries (it open-codes attempt/delay_ms/MAX_RETRIES), so it escaped both the fix and the repo invariant `every_retry_call_site_derives_its_idempotency_class` (trust.rs:160: files without `with_retries(` are skipped). Every cmdlet here is a POST, and the crate's own writes are not replay-safe: a replayed `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` (rbac.rs:232-246) after a committed write fails as a duplicate, which grants.rs:118 records as `failed to assign` -> role_in_place=false -> targets_safe_to_strip keeps the org-wide grant, so the scope silently has no effect (the exact failure mode RoleStep::SameRoleAs was added to prevent). A replayed `Remove-ApplicationAccessPolicy` (rbac.rs:277-284) after a committed delete returns a not-found 400, which aap_migration.rs:371-376 reports as `failed to remove legacy policy` and status `partial` while the policy is actually gone. `New-ServicePrincipal`, `New-ManagementScope`, `New-DistributionGroup`, `Remove-ManagementRoleAssignment` and `Remove-DistributionGroup` have the same exposure.
findings.proposal: Rewrite send_core around `azapptoolkit_core::http_retry::with_retries("exchange", class, |_| ...)` returning `Attempt<Bytes, ExchangeError>` (Retry{Throttled} on 429, Retry{Transient} on 5xx/send error, Done otherwise). Derive `class` from the cmdlet verb in a `retry_class_for_cmdlet(cmdlet: &str) -> RetryClass` helper in transport.rs: `Get-*`/`Test-*` -> Idempotent; `Set-ManagementScope` and the two membership mutators the client already makes idempotent (add_group_member/remove_group_member swallow already-/not-a-member) -> Idempotent; everything else (`New-*`, `Remove-*`) -> NonIdempotent. Have invoke_command pass the class through. Extend the trust.rs invariant so a crate whose transport sends HTTP without `with_retries(` is itself an offender (today the exchange crate is silently skipped). Add wiremock tests: `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` 502 -> exactly one request (`.expect(1)`), `Get-ManagementScope` 502 then 200 -> two requests.

findings.title: Mid-pagination errors are flattened to Protocol, losing auth/throttle classification and the re-auth-fatal signal
findings.rationale: The comment justifies the reclassification only for NotFound (so invoke_optional cannot read a 404 on page 2 as an empty collection), but the arm catches every error. A `Token` error carrying `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in` from the bearer() call on page 2 becomes `protocol_error`, so `is_reauth_fatal` is false and a long-running fan-out (the audit's Exchange probes, bulk remediations) keeps going on a dead session, contrary to the AGENTS.md invariant that every long-running loop stops on a re-auth-fatal code. Likewise a 401/403/429 on page 2 no longer matches the audit's Exchange breaker or ui_hint branches; the operator sees a generic protocol error instead of the stale-token guidance.
findings.proposal: Narrow the arm: reclassify to Protocol only `ExchangeError::NotFound(_)` and `ExchangeError::Api { body, .. } if is_not_found_body(&body)`; return every other error unchanged (they already prevent a truncated Ok). Add two wiremock tests: page-2 401 -> `ExchangeError::Unauthorized`; page-2 StaticTokenProvider failure with code refresh_missing -> `ui_code() == "refresh_missing"`.

findings.title: ExchangeError is hand-rolled outside core::http_error_enum! and has no error-conformance test, contradicting AGENTS.md
findings.rationale: Graph, ARM and Key Vault errors are generated by the macro; ARM and Key Vault additionally carry `tests/error_conformance.rs` pinning that every variant's `ui_code`/`is_retryable` agree with core. The Exchange enum is the fourth copy the macro's own doc says the refactor 'did not reach', kept separate because `Forbidden` carries `had_diagnostics`. The `.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:24` wording ("Graph/ARM/Key Vault error taxonomy") is honest about the gap but AGENTS.md is not, and there is nothing pinning that Exchange's `ui_code` table (error.rs:64-81) stays aligned with the shared codes the frontend branches on.
findings.proposal: Either (a) extend `http_error_enum!` with an optional `forbidden = { ... }` override (or express the reasonless 403 as an `extra` variant `ForbiddenReasonless(String) => "forbidden"`), then define ExchangeError through the macro keeping only `ui_hint` and `is_missing_object` inline; or (b) if the struct-variant Forbidden must stay, add `crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/tests/error_conformance.rs` mirroring the ARM one (every variant -> `ui_code`, `is_retryable == is_retryable_code(ui_code)`, Token passthrough) and amend AGENTS.md:108 to say "Graph/ARM/Key Vault". Option (a) also removes the risk that a new shared code is added to the macro and not here.

findings.title: Tenant-wide list reads that gate the irreversible group delete use invoke_optional, so a misclassified 400 reads as 'no references'
findings.rationale: invoke_optional exists so an `-Identity` that does not resolve reads as None. An identity-less `Get-ManagementScope`/`Get-ApplicationAccessPolicy` has no object to be missing: an empty tenant returns 200 with `value: []`. Routing them through invoke_optional means any 400 whose sanitized body happens to contain "not found"/"couldn't be found" (a parameter set that cannot be resolved, a cmdlet the caller's role does not expose, an EXO wording change) becomes `Ok(vec![])`. `retired_scope_groups` then reports `reference_check_complete: true` and `delete_exchange_scope_group` re-checks live through the same path and finds zero references - exactly the 'unknown read as clean' the docs say must never happen. `list_service_principals` (rbac.rs:59-64) already uses invoke_command, so the two list-alls are also inconsistent with their sibling.
findings.proposal: Switch `list_management_scopes` and `get_application_access_policies` to `invoke_command` (keep `get_management_scope`/`get_service_principal`/`get_group`, which take an Identity, on invoke_optional). Add a wiremock test: `Get-ManagementScope` with `{}` returning 400 "...not found..." must be `Err(ExchangeError::Api{..})`, not `Ok(vec![])`. Optionally tighten `is_not_found_body` to require the cmdlet-shaped phrasings ("couldn't be found", "ManagementObjectNotFound") and drop the bare "not found".

findings.title: DN set comparisons are case-sensitive in the consolidation path but case-folded in the post-write proof, so a landed repoint can be reported as a mismatch
findings.evidence:
repoint: !(source_dns.len() == 1 && source_dns[0] == managed_dn),
-- targets.rs:480-486 (same file): "Exchange Online normalises the casing of the DNs it returns ... a case-sensitive HashSet comparison of 'what I wrote' against 'what the server reports' can differ on a write that DID land." rbac.rs:197 `if wanted_groups.folded_dns() != landed.folded_dns()`; but scope_group.rs:540 `g.complete && g.dns == group_dns_in_filter(wanted)` and scope_group.rs:744 `&& source_dns[0] == dn`.
findings.rationale: The crate documents (targets.rs:480-486, aap_migration.rs:288-292) that Exchange echoes DNs in its own casing and that the post-write proof must fold case for that reason, yet `plan_consolidation` and both desktop consumers of the same DN sets compare raw strings. Consequences: (1) in `reconcile_scope_filter` (aap_migration) the repoint passes rbac.rs's folded proof, then `scope_filter_agrees` compares unfolded and returns `scope_filter_mismatch`, refusing an app whose scope is correct; (2) in `move_exchange_scope_to_managed_group`, a scope already on the managed group with a case-different echoed DN skips the early return at :744, is 'repointed' again, and `retired_scope_groups(&source_dns)` then lists the app's own managed group as a retired cleanup candidate (only the downstream `identity.matches(&managed)` guard in delete stops the deletion).
findings.proposal: Add one helper in the crate, e.g. `ScopeGroups::same_groups_as(&self, other: &ScopeGroups) -> bool` (both complete and `folded_dns()` equal) plus `pub fn same_dn(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool` (ASCII-fold), and use them at targets.rs:716, scope_group.rs:540 and :744. Extend `consolidation_is_a_no_op_when_the_scope_is_already_managed` with a case-variant DN. Consider `to_lowercase()` instead of `to_ascii_lowercase()` in `folded_dns` so a `CN=Zürich…` DN folds too.

findings.title: exchange-scoping.md still documents the deleted value-only scoping functions and a moved helper path
findings.evidence:
the value-only `exchange_role_for_permission` exists for the probe/badge paths and is unambiguous
-- :49 "it widens `is_scopable_exchange_permission`"; :123-124 "`held_orgwide_mail_grants` filters with the **value-only** `is_scopable_exchange_permission`"; :141 "sanitized (`client.rs::sanitize_error_body`)".
-- roles.rs:11-13: "Only the resource-aware forms exist to re-export now: the value-only ones were deleted"; repo_invariants/commands.rs:130-134 pins `exchange_role_for_permission` / `is_scopable_exchange_permission` as GONE; sanitize_error_body now lives at client/transport.rs:293.
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md says to read this deep-dive before editing the subsystem. It tells the reader that two functions exist and are the right tool for the probe/badge paths, while a repo-invariant test fails the build if anyone reintroduces them; a contributor following the doc will write code the test rejects. The `client.rs::sanitize_error_body` path is stale since the client was split into client/{transport,rbac,groups}.rs.
findings.proposal: Rewrite :29-34 to name `exchange_role_for_resource_permission` / `is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission` and state that the value-only forms were removed (link the invariant). At :49 and :123-124 name the resource-aware gate and, for `held_orgwide_mail_grants`, describe what it actually does today. Change :141 to `client/transport.rs::sanitize_error_body`.

findings.title: set_management_scope_filter's pre-write refusals, ensure_management_scope's create path and the transport's 5xx/network paths have no wiremock tests
findings.rationale: These refusals are the only thing standing between a caller and 'widen every role assignment on the scope to the whole organization'; the comments say 'no caller does' is not a property the function may rely on, yet nothing proves the refusal happens before the cmdlet is issued. Similarly `ensure_management_scope` (create-only, the invariant AGENTS.md names) has no test that the Get-first/New-second sequence runs or that an existing scope suppresses `New-ManagementScope`. The transport's retry-then-`Server`/`Network`/`Throttled` terminal mappings (transport.rs:273-282) are likewise untested; only the 429-then-200 happy path is.
findings.proposal: Add to client/tests.rs: (1) empty filter and `-like` filter each -> `Protocol` with a `Set-ManagementScope` mock carrying `.expect(0)`; (2) `ensure_management_scope` creates when `Get-ManagementScope` returns `[]` and skips `New-` when it returns a scope; (3) 503 x4 -> `ExchangeError::Server`, reqwest connect error -> `Network`, 429 x4 -> `Throttled{retry_after_secs}`. About 120 lines, all following the existing mock pattern.

findings.title: Desktop commands/exchange/tests.rs duplicates the crate's pure-function tests in the slowest-to-build crate
findings.rationale: verdict.rs's module doc explains the logic was moved into the crate precisely so it is testable without a Tauri State; the desktop tests that predate the move were left behind (a few are marked '---- relocated ----' in the crate, the rest were copied not moved). Roughly 15 of the 33 desktop tests (lines 81-190, 234-350, 363-470, 532-590) exercise only crate-pure functions with their own fixtures, so every rule now has two fixture sets that can drift, and they run only in `apps/desktop/src-tauri`, which cannot compile without WebKitGTK and is the slowest `just test-crate` target.
findings.proposal: Delete the duplicates from the desktop tests and keep only those exercising desktop glue (`resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached`, `retired_groups_note_*`, `scope_filter_agrees` via `a_divergent_or_unreadable_scope_filter_is_never_agreement`, `migration_keeps_the_policy_*`, `scope_and_group_names_*`, `alias_is_safe_and_bounded`). Where a desktop test covers an angle the crate test does not (e.g. `reconcile_lets_a_surviving_ews_grant_defeat_every_scope` already has a twin), fold the extra assertion into the crate test first.

findings.title: AccessRight and ScopeType are stringly typed and compared by literal in several places
findings.evidence:
#[serde(rename = "AccessRight", default)]
pub access_right: Option<String>,
-- aap.rs:60-61: `match policy.access_right.as_deref().map(str::trim) { Some(right) if right.eq_ignore_ascii_case("RestrictAccess") => {}`
-- verdict.rs:131-133: `p.access_right.as_deref().is_some_and(|r| r.eq_ignore_ascii_case("RestrictAccess"))`
-- verdict.rs:34-42: `matches!(r.scope_type ... "" | "notapplicable" | "organizationconfig" | "organizationscope" | "organization")`
findings.rationale: The RestrictAccess-vs-DenyAccess distinction is the single most consequential decision in the migration (a DenyAccess policy must never be inverted) and it is spelled as a case-insensitive string comparison in two modules that each had to independently remember to trim and casefold (the aap.rs doc notes 'this one did not' for an earlier casefold miss). models.rs already has the tolerant-deserializer pattern (`ps_access_check`, `ps_optional_bool`) for exactly this shape.
findings.proposal: Add `pub enum AapAccessRight { RestrictAccess, DenyAccess, Unknown(String) }` with a tolerant `deserialize_with` (trim + eq_ignore_ascii_case), `is_restrict()`, and use it in `group_policies_for_migration` and `aap_verdict_for`; likewise `enum ExoScopeType { NotApplicable, Organization, CustomRecipientScope, AdministrativeUnit, Other(String) }` for `is_org_wide_auth_row`. The two `eq_ignore_ascii_case("RestrictAccess")` sites collapse to one match, and the 'unreadable AccessRight' branch becomes `Unknown(_)`.

findings.title: Cargo.toml declares unused `url` and `tokio` dependencies and a per-crate `bytes` instead of a workspace dependency
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md: 'Workspace dependency - add to [workspace.dependencies], use name.workspace = true ... Dependencies are a cost'. `url` and `tokio` in [dependencies] are dead (tokio is only needed by the `#[tokio::test]`s, and it is already re-declared with features under [dev-dependencies]); `bytes` is the one HTTP-client dependency not centralised, so a version bump is a four-file edit.
findings.proposal: Remove `url` and `tokio` from [dependencies] (keep the dev-dependency), add `bytes = "1"` to the root [workspace.dependencies] and switch the four crates to `bytes.workspace = true`. Consider adding `cargo udeps` (or `cargo machete`) to `just verify-full` to catch this class.

findings.title: No teardown for the management scope and Exchange SP pointer after access removal, so the create-only scope pins any future re-grant
findings.rationale: An operator who removes an app's scoped Exchange access (or decommissions the app) is left with an orphaned `app_scope_<appId>` scope, an SP pointer and a managed group. Because `ensure_management_scope` is create-only by design, re-granting later with a different group set hits the `scope_group_mismatch` refusal (grants.rs:245-258) until someone deletes the stale scope by hand in PowerShell - the one thing this toolkit exists to replace. The crate already has the enumeration primitives (`get_role_assignments`, `list_management_scopes`, `references_to_group`) needed to prove the scope is unreferenced before deleting it.
findings.proposal: Add `ExchangeClient::remove_management_scope(name)` (`Remove-ManagementScope -Identity -Confirm:$false`) and `remove_service_principal(identity)` to rbac.rs, each preceded in the command layer by a live proof: zero `Get-ManagementRoleAssignment -CustomResourceScope <name>` rows (or a filter over `list`), and for the pointer zero remaining assignments for the app. Expose them as an opt-in `also_remove_scope_and_pointer: bool` on `remove_exchange_mailbox_access`, defaulting false, and reuse the existing typed-confirmation UI pattern from `delete_exchange_scope_group`. CHANGELOG entry required (user-visible).

The line-count history is wrong since the split. The three intra-doc links resolve to nothing in this crate and produce `rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links` warnings under `cargo doc`.
findings.proposal: Replace the NOTE with a one-line statement that `beta/InvokeCommand` is the endpoint the ExchangeOnlineManagement module uses (versus the per-cmdlet `v2.0/<Cmdlet>` REST routes Microsoft documents separately). Trim the two 'lived in a 3,100-line file' paragraphs to 'moved out of the command layer so it is testable without a Tauri State'. Change the three links to plain code spans naming the module: `commands::exchange::mail_scopes::legacy_aap_scope`.

If finding 1 is deferred, remove the method or add a `#[cfg(test)]` assertion that mirrors the ARM conformance test.

result.coverage_notes: Read fully: every file in crates/azapptoolkit-exchange (Cargo.toml, lib.rs, roles.rs, client.rs, client/transport.rs, client/rbac.rs, client/groups.rs, client/tests.rs, error.rs, models.rs, aap.rs, references.rs, targets.rs, verdict.rs) and docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md. Read partially, only to verify call sites and consequences: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/exchange/{mod,grants,aap_migration,scope_group,tests}.rs, state.rs, permission_tester.rs, tests/repo_invariants/{trust,commands}.rs, crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/{http_retry,http_error,reauth,token,cloud}.rs and the graph transport around with_retries. Did not run cargo build/test/clippy/doc (per instructions); the rustdoc broken-link claim is by inspection of the link targets, not a `cargo doc` run. Could not confirm from Microsoft Learn whether `Get-ManagementRoleAssignment` output exposes the scope as `CustomResourceScope` (the property `roles_already_scoped` keys on); the RBAC-for-Applications doc examples show only the Format-Table default columns, so this was not reported as a defect.

result.area_summary: The three small crates are tidy and well-tested at the transport level: the shared `http_error_enum!`/`http_retry` policy is applied consistently, origin guards on `nextLink` and `role_definition_id` are in place, secret material has redacted `Debug` and a zeroizing write request, and both leaf crates carry conformance tests pinning retryability and re-auth passthrough. The weaknesses are semantic rather than mechanical: the ARM client documents `atScope()` as "direct only" when Azure defines it as "at or above" (so the Key Vault reverse lookup labels inherited subscription Owners as direct vault grants), the Log Analytics client silently accepts a `PartialError` 200 as a complete result, and Key Vault `set_secret` (a versioning PUT) is classed idempotent and replayed after 5xx despite the crate's own comment naming exactly that hazard. The permissions crate is a 6-entry resource directory that still carries a full permission-catalog type surface, an always-miss `lookup_permission`, and docs (AGENTS.md, README, rules) that describe a catalog that no longer exists; ARM and Key Vault also keep two byte-identical ~90-line transport loops that the macro-generated error enums make easy to unify in core.

findings.title: `atScope()` is documented as excluding inherited assignments; Azure defines it as "at or above the scope" — the Key Vault reverse lookup labels inherited subscription/RG roles as direct vault grants
findings.rationale: The doc comment, the sweep's module doc, the DTO doc and two user-facing strings all assert the opposite of the documented ARM semantics. `atScope()` at a vault path returns the vault's own assignments PLUS every assignment inherited from its resource group, subscription, management group and root — the very "inherited subscription Owner" rows the comment says are excluded. The operator is told these are explicit vault grants and the panel's empty-state text claims inherited-only vaults "won't appear here", so the least-privilege picture is misreported (a subscription Owner is shown as a per-vault grant; a vault that is only reachable via inheritance shows rows anyway). `high_privilege` flags then fire on rows the user was told are direct.
findings.proposal: Keep the `atScope()` query (it is the correct single call) but stop calling the rows direct: in `sweep_key_vault_access` compare `props.scope` to the vault `id` case-insensitively and either drop non-matching rows or add `inherited: bool` to `KeyVaultAccessRow` and render an "inherited from <scope level>" badge. Rewrite the doc comment at client.rs:90-94 to "at or above `scope`", fix keyvault_rbac.rs:5 / dto keyvault.rs:16 / the two UI strings (keyvault.rs:245, 354), and add a wiremock test in client.rs where one assignment's `scope` is the subscription and assert the consumer classifies it as inherited. Expected effect: the panel answers the question it claims to answer, and the "direct" label stops being wrong for every inherited Owner.

findings.title: Log Analytics `PartialError` responses (HTTP 200 + `error`) are treated as complete results — the granted-vs-used analysis can be built on truncated/failed query output
findings.rationale: `usage.rs::get_app_graph_usage` turns the first table into `GraphUsageResult` and the UI uses it to recommend permission downgrades ("only GETs observed → Downgrade applies"). A runaway/timeout/truncation on a large 90-day `summarize` yields 200 with partial rows and an `error.code == "PartialError"`; the model discards `error`, so the panel shows fewer call patterns than exist and the operator may strip a permission the app actually uses. The DTO already models coverage honesty for `truncated` but has no channel for this case.
findings.proposal: Add `#[serde(default)] pub error: Option<LogsErrorInfo { code: String, message: String }>` to `LogsQueryResponse`; in `LogAnalyticsClient::query` return `Err(ArmError::Protocol(format!("partial result: {code}: {message}")))` when `error` is present (or return `(table, partial: bool)` and thread a `partial` flag into `GraphUsageResult` beside `truncated` so the panel warns instead of failing). Add a wiremock test with `{"tables":[...],"error":{"code":"PartialError",...}}`. Effect: a degraded query can no longer read as an all-clear usage picture.

findings.title: Key Vault `set_secret` (PUT) is classed `Idempotent` and replayed after a 5xx/network error, but each `PUT /secrets/{name}` creates a new version — the crate's own comment names this exact hazard
findings.rationale: `setSecret` is the PUT this function routes to `Idempotent`, yet the doc comment cites `setSecret` as the example of a write that must not be replayed. Key Vault's SET operation always appends a version, so a 502/connection reset after the service committed is replayed up to `MAX_RETRIES` times and leaves duplicate versions of the rotated client secret in the vault (and, on final failure, `rotate_app_credential` removes the app secret while a vault version already holds it). Same class of defect the core `RetryClass` doc records for `addPassword`. The repo invariant in `tests/repo_invariants/trust.rs:167` only requires the file to contain `retry_class_for(`, so a Key Vault-specific mapping is compliant.
findings.proposal: In `retry_class_for` route `Method::PUT` to `RetryClass::NonIdempotent` for this crate (Key Vault PUTs version, they don't upsert) and correct the doc comment; alternatively pass the class explicitly from `set_secret` through `send_json`. Add a wiremock test: first PUT answers 502, assert exactly one PUT was received and the error is `Server`. Expected effect: a transient failure during rotation produces at most one vault version and a clear error instead of silent duplicates.

findings.title: `principalId eq` returns assignments "at, above or below" each subscription, so a management-group/root assignment is returned once per subscription and rendered as N duplicate rows
findings.rationale: The client doc says "at or below" but ARM also returns assignments *above* the subscription (management groups, tenant root). A managed identity with Reader on a management group over 20 subscriptions appears 20 times in `list_managed_identity_azure_roles`, each row labelled with a different `subscription` display name, inflating the Azure RBAC footprint and the high-privilege count the operator sees. `readiness.rs` is unaffected (collects into a `HashSet` of GUIDs).
findings.proposal: Fix the doc comment to "at, above or below" and dedupe in the consumer by `RoleAssignment.id` (a `HashSet<String>` before `flat`), labelling above-subscription rows with the scope rather than the subscription that surfaced them. Add a unit test with two subscriptions returning the same MG-scoped assignment id and assert one row. Effort small; effect: no phantom duplicate roles.

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/keyvault.rs:35-47 maps only name/id/enabled/expires/content_type into `KvSecretItemDto`.
findings.rationale: Every Key Vault certificate materialises a `managed: true` secret in `GET /secrets`. The browser lists them like any other secret, and the rotation dialog's secret-name field can be pointed at one; Key Vault refuses `set` on a managed secret, so the operator gets a raw `vault error (400/403)` after the new app secret was already minted (then rolled back). Surfacing `managed` costs one field and lets the UI badge/exclude those rows. The list response also carries `attributes.recoveryLevel`/`recoverableDays`, useful for the same panel.
findings.proposal: Add `#[serde(default)] pub managed: Option<bool>` to `SecretItem` and `managed: Option<bool>` to `KvSecretItemDto`; render a "certificate-backed" badge in `key_vault_view.rs` and filter managed names out of the rotation target picker. Add a wiremock fixture with `"managed": true`.

findings.title: `KeyVaultResource` drops `properties.enableRbacAuthorization`, so the RBAC sweep cannot tell a legacy access-policy vault from one with no assignments — the UI admits both "produce no rows"
findings.rationale: The ARM vault list already returns `properties.enableRbacAuthorization` on every item; discarding it means the sweep's coverage numbers (`vaults_scanned`) count access-policy vaults as scanned-and-empty, when in fact their access model is invisible to `roleAssignments`. For a security posture surface that is a silent gap: an operator sees 40 scanned vaults and 12 with rows and cannot tell which of the other 28 are governed by access policies (a finding in itself — AGENTS/capabilities treat legacy mode as a problem).
findings.proposal: Add `properties: Option<KeyVaultResourceProperties { enable_rbac_authorization: Option<bool> }>` to `KeyVaultResource`; in `sweep_key_vault_access` skip the roleAssignments read for `false` vaults, count them in a new `vaults_access_policy_mode` field on `KeyVaultSweepResult`, and show it beside `vaults_failed` in the panel (optionally as a Security-tab finding "vault uses legacy access policies"). Wiremock test for the property.

findings.title: The permissions catalog carries no permission data, leaving `lookup_permission`, the catalog rung of the resolution ladder, and the permission entry types as dead code
findings.rationale: The crate deliberately became a 6-row resource directory (module doc says so), but it still ships `AppRoleEntry`, `ScopeEntry`, `allowed_member_types` with a comment about "older catalog snapshots", `CatalogRoot.generated/version` that nothing reads, a `lookup_permission` that can only return `None` (and is pinned by a test to do so), a 34-line unreachable "1. Catalog" branch in `resolve_one_permission`, and `list_catalog_resources` reporting `role_count`/`scope_count` that are always 0 (the picker ignores them and uses `list_resource_permission_counts`). This is exactly the docs-in-code-contradicts-code smell: a reader of `permissions_resolve.rs` believes a bundled fallback exists offline.
findings.proposal: Pick one direction. (a) Honest directory: rename the type to `ResourceDirectory`, delete `AppRoleEntry`/`ScopeEntry`/`lookup_permission`/`CatalogRoot.generated|version`, remove ladder step 1 and the `role_count`/`scope_count` fields from `list_catalog_resources` (or fill them from the live counts). (b) Real catalog: add a `just permissions-refresh` recipe that regenerates `catalog.json` from `GET /servicePrincipals?$filter=appId in (…)` and keep the ladder. (a) is the smaller, lower-risk change and matches the crate's current intent.

findings.title: AGENTS.md, the Claude rules file, README and the Permissions tab header describe a bundled permissions catalog with Graph fallback "for unknown resources"; the code resolves every permission live and bundles only six resource names
findings.rationale: Four documents tell agents and users that permission names come from a bundled catalog and that Graph is a fallback for unknown *resources*; the crate doc and code say the opposite (names come from Graph for every resource; the bundle only seeds the dropdown). An agent following AGENTS.md would look for permission GUIDs in `data/` to add a rule; a user reading the README expects offline permission browsing. Staleness surfaces to users as an unexplained empty picker when Graph is unreachable.
findings.proposal: Reword AGENTS.md:112 and rules:29 to "`azapptoolkit-permissions` bundles only a resource *directory* (six first-party appIds/names) for the picker dropdown; every permission definition is resolved live via `resolve_resource_sp()` and cached under `CacheKind::Permissions`." Fix README.md:75-77 and the permissions_tab.rs header accordingly.

findings.title: Frontend DTOs and a binding struct exist for a `kv_set_secret` command that has no backend, and the crate advertises `delete_secret` that does not exist — while the operator-roles docs promise full secret CRUD
findings.rationale: Half-built plumbing (a request DTO with redacted Debug, a metadata response DTO, a binding args struct) sits behind a `#![allow(dead_code)]` and a doc comment naming a command that never existed, and the recommended custom Azure role grants `deleteSecret` for an operation the app cannot perform. An Entra admin who lands a rotated secret in a vault has no way to create a plain secret or clean one up from the toolkit — the crate is one PUT/DELETE away from both.
findings.proposal: Either implement it: add `KeyVaultClient::delete_secret(name)` (DELETE, idempotent) and a `kv_set_secret` command using the existing `KvSetSecretInput` (parse `expires` RFC3339 → `SecretAttributesRequest`), register in `generate_handler!`, add the binding fn and a "New secret" / "Delete" action in `key_vault_view.rs`, plus demo fixtures; or remove `KvSetSecretInput`, `KvSecretMetadataDto`, `SetArgs`, and fix lib.rs:10 and OPERATOR-ROLES.md:31. Implementing is M; removing is S.

findings.rationale: Built-in role definitions (`Owner`, `Reader`, `Key Vault Secrets Officer`…) share one GUID across every subscription but each subscription-prefixed path is a distinct cache key, so a 30-subscription estate resolves `Owner` 30 times per sweep and stores 30 cache entries. The 30-line block is copy-pasted, so the caching rules ("only a real name is cached") can drift between the MI view and the vault sweep; the two hard-coded privilege name lists overlap and neither lives with the role knowledge in core.
findings.proposal: Create `commands/arm_roles.rs::resolve_role_names(arm: &ArmClient, cache, tenant_id, ids: HashSet<String>) -> HashMap<String,String>` keyed by `azure_roles::role_id_tail(id)`, fetching each GUID once (prefer the tenant-level `/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions/{guid}` path for built-ins); move `HIGH_PRIVILEGE_ROLES`/`KV_HIGH_PRIVILEGE_ROLES` to `core::azure_roles` as one table with a `is_high_privilege(name, context)` helper. Both commands call the helper.

findings.title: `LogAnalyticsClient::query` and the ARM list calls splice server-supplied ids (`customerId`, `subscriptionId`) into URL paths with no structural check, unlike `get_role_definition` which refuses the same class
findings.rationale: The crate's own reasoning treats ARM response fields as attacker-influenced and refuses `?`/`#`/authority tricks for `role_definition_id`, but `customerId` and `subscriptionId` (also ARM output) reach `format!` unchecked: `?`/`#` would inject or truncate the query and `../` segments are normalised by `url`, redirecting the call to a different same-origin path. Severity is low because the value follows a `/`, so the authority cannot change and the bearer stays on-origin; the exposure is path/query rewriting with the operator's own token.
findings.proposal: Add `fn require_guid(s: &str) -> Result<()>` (36 chars, hex + hyphens) in `azapptoolkit-arm` and apply it to `workspace_customer_id`, every `subscription_id` parameter, and `principal_id` (currently only quote-escaped), returning `ArmError::Protocol`. Unit-test with `sub?api-version=x`, `../providers/…`, and a valid GUID.

findings.title: `Subscription` drops the `state` field, so Disabled/Warned/Deleted subscriptions are fanned out to and their failures counted as coverage gaps (`skipped`) or logged as warnings
findings.rationale: ARM's `/subscriptions` returns `state` (Enabled, Warned, PastDue, Disabled, Deleted). Reads against a Disabled/Deleted subscription fail, so every sweep (`list_managed_identity_azure_roles`, `sweep_key_vault_access`, `list_available_key_vaults`, `enumerate_azure_role_ids`, `discover_workspace`) pays a round trip, logs a warning, and reports the subscription as a coverage failure the operator cannot act on. Filtering up front makes `skipped`/`vaults_failed` mean what their docs say.
findings.proposal: Add `#[serde(default)] pub state: Option<String>` to `Subscription`; in the five consumers, partition out `state != Some("Enabled")` before the fan-out and report them separately (e.g. `subscriptions_inactive: usize`) instead of counting them as failures. One-line wiremock assertion in `lists_subscriptions`.

findings.title: ARM 409 `RoleAssignmentExists` on `create_role_assignment` reaches the operator as a raw `arm error (409): {json}`
findings.rationale: Re-assigning a role the identity already holds at that scope is the most common operator slip in this dialog; ARM answers 409 with `{"error":{"code":"RoleAssignmentExists",...}}`, and the user sees a JSON blob under the generic `arm_error` code with no retry/no guidance. The client exposes enough (`Api{status:409, body}`) to classify it.
findings.proposal: In `assign_managed_identity_azure_role`, match `ArmError::Api { status: 409, body }` whose body contains `RoleAssignmentExists` and return `UiError::validation("already_assigned", "This identity already holds that role at this scope.")` (or treat as success and refresh the list). Add a unit test on the mapping. Optionally have the ARM client parse the `error.code` field into `Api` for all 4xx so callers stop substring-matching JSON.

findings.title: Stale Key Vault crate comments: header claims no shared retry code while importing `core::http_retry`, `lib.rs` lists a nonexistent `delete_secret`, and `get_secret`'s `version` is unvalidated and never used by any caller
findings.rationale: The header contradicts the very imports beneath it (the loop was moved to core in the PR the module-level docs elsewhere cite), the crate doc advertises an operation that does not exist, and `version` is a path segment that skips the `validate_secret_name`-style guard the module doc says exists for "anything that flows into request URLs" — harmless today only because no caller passes it.
findings.proposal: Rewrite client.rs:3-6 to say the loop is `core::http_retry::with_retries` and only per-attempt status mapping is local; fix lib.rs:10; either drop the `version` parameter or validate it (32 lowercase hex chars) in `validate.rs` with a test. Also drop the unused `Serialize` derive on `Paged<T>` (models.rs:165).

findings.title: `SecretValue` derives `Serialize` although nothing serialises it, so the redacted `Debug` can be bypassed by any future `serde_json::to_string`/JSON tracing field
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/models.rs:40-43
/// `GET /secrets/{name}` — full value included.
#[derive(Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SecretValue {
    pub value: String,

models.rs:53-54 "/// Manual impl so a stray `{:?}` can't log the secret value"

`grep -rn SecretValue apps crates` outside the crate: only `KvSecretValueDto` (the IPC DTO) is used; no call serialises `SecretValue`.
findings.rationale: The workspace treats a derived `Debug` on a secret-bearing type as a defect and hand-writes redaction, but a derived `Serialize` gives an equally direct plaintext path (`tracing` JSON layers, `serde_json::to_string` in a future export/backup) that no test guards. Since the IPC boundary uses `KvSecretValueDto`, the derive is unused surface.
findings.proposal: Remove `Serialize` from `SecretValue` (keep `Deserialize`); if a serialiser is ever needed, implement it manually with the value redacted or gated. Consider the same for `KvSecretValueDto` if the IPC path can move to a redacted transport in future.

findings.title: Both crates declare `tracing` but never use it, list `tokio` as a runtime dependency used only by `#[tokio::test]`, and pin `bytes = "1"` outside `[workspace.dependencies]`
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/Cargo.toml:13-20
tokio = { workspace = true }
bytes = "1"
...
tracing = { workspace = true }

crates/azapptoolkit-arm/Cargo.toml:13-19 (same three lines)

`grep -rn "tracing" crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src` → no matches

findings.proposal: Delete `tracing` from both `[dependencies]`; move `tokio` to `[dev-dependencies]` only (it stays available transitively via reqwest at runtime); add `bytes = "1"` to `[workspace.dependencies]` and reference it with `workspace = true`. verdicts.corrected_title: Rule 13 emits the broad-prefix delegated advisory for declared scopes regardless of consent; the group blurb and predicate doc promise admin-consented ones
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Thread the per-client AllPrincipals scope set the runner already keeps (audit.rs:914-931, `delegated_scopes_by_client`) into app rows too, so the rule can tell an admin-consented scope from a merely declared, user-consentable one; keep the two PS entries unconditional; emit the broad-prefix half only for consented scopes, or word it separately ("declared" vs "admin-consented"). Do NOT gate on the coarse `has_admin_consent` flag alone: the grants read is best-effort (audit.rs:933-939) and a failed read would silently hide the advisory, against the over-report-is-safe stance at permissions.rs:194-197. Fix groups.rs:113 to match whatever the rule actually reports, and add the table rows.
verdicts.notes: Premise verified: scoring.rs:480-484 filters `perms.scope_values` with `is_risky_delegated_scope` and never reads `has_admin_consent`; for app rows `scope_values` is the declared manifest (audit.rs:1475); permissions.rs:167-169 says "when admin-consented"; groups.rs:113 blurb says "Admin-consented delegated scopes"; the widening comment at scoring.rs:471-479 and CHANGELOG-archive:377-381 frame the change around admin-consented scopes; the only Rule-13 table (tests.rs:399-403) has three rows. Overstated: for SP rows `scope_values` IS the AllPrincipals grant set (audit.rs:1264-1267), so the blurb is right there; and the proposed `has_admin_consent` gate is app-level, not per-scope, and fails silent when the tenant-wide grants read fails. Advisory only (no score), so medium is for group noise/mislabeling, not ranking.

verdicts.corrected_title: `Calendars.ReadWrite` keeps its PS-ported medium weight while the net-new `Contacts.ReadWrite` is high — reconcile or document the exception

A guard test asserting every mailbox-family `*.ReadWrite` in `graph_mail_role` is HIGH would fail today, so it needs the same `INTENTIONALLY_*` exemption pattern the file already uses (permissions.rs:660-668).
verdicts.notes: Inconsistency is real: permissions.rs:105-108 states write=high/read=medium, MailboxSettings.ReadWrite (113) and Contacts.ReadWrite (123) are HIGH, Calendars.ReadWrite (145) is MEDIUM; `mailbox_family_risk_entries_agree_with_the_scoping_role_map` (602-637) only checks spelling. But it is not a bug: the medium list "Mirrors Constants.ps1:123-130" (129-130), the entry's own comment says it sat there "for its whole life" (137-145), CHANGELOG-archive:366-375 fixed only the plural typo and kept the tier, and mod.rs:3-6 says every constant matches the legacy module. The write=high sentence at 105-108 describes how the *net-new* additions were weighted. So this is a PS-parity vs net-new consistency question — a risk-model call, not a defect.

Verified: MEDIUM list (permissions.rs:131-157) contains Mail.Read, Files.Read.All, Sites.Read.All, User/Group.Read.All, Directory.Read.All, Chat.Read.All, Calendars.Read — not Contacts.Read, MailboxSettings.Read, Device.Read.All, Notes.Read.All, Application.Read.All (nor GroupMember.Read.All / RoleManagement.Read.Directory). Premise holds end to end. `check_for_update` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/updater.rs:26-37) calls `app.updater().check()` unconditionally; `perform_update` (43-72) likewise. `UserSettings::load` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:82-88) is the only place `auto_update_env_override` is applied and its only callers are the module's own tests (251, 259, 267); every production reader uses `UserSettings::stored` (state.rs:234, 376; commands/defaults.rs:19; commands/exchange/mod.rs:74). `grep auto_update|AUTO_UPDATE` under apps/ (rs/json/toml) returns nothing, so no binding, command, or view consults the field; the frontend launch effect (web-rs/src/views/shell.rs:164-176) and the manual button (186-200) both fire unconditionally. Expose the policy to the frontend (e.g. an `update_policy` command, or fold a `disabled_by_policy` flag into the check result) so shell.rs hides or disables the manual 'Check for updates' item with a reason rather than toasting a misleading 'You're on the latest version'. Add a settings.rs test that `load` honours `AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE` (the existing tests deliberately avoid the env var), a src-tauri test that the two updater commands short-circuit when `auto_update == false`, and a `demo::register_fixtures` entry if a new infallible invoke is introduced.
