verdicts.notes: The mechanism is real: crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/client/transport.rs:11-14 imports only the raw primitives, and `send_core` retries every POST on a reqwest error (181-188) and on 429/5xx (265-270) up to `MAX_RETRIES` with no `RetryClass`; `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` (rbac.rs:243), `New-ServicePrincipal` (rbac.rs:31), `New-ManagementScope` (rbac.rs:80), `Remove-ManagementRoleAssignment` (rbac.rs:260) all ride it. The `trust.rs` invariant (apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/trust.rs:163) skips any file without `with_retries(`, so the loop is invisible to it; commit 8fb1ac7 (the RetryClass fix) touched transport.rs only for the same-origin check, and its CHANGELOG entry (CHANGELOG.md:504-515) claims 'the transports route everything through it'. No Exchange test covers a 5xx/network replay (only `retry_after_is_honored_on_429`, tests.rs:492). This is a genuine gap against AGENTS.md's 'one definition per policy' rule. But the headline harm is refuted by the repo's own code: (a) a duplicate `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` for the same role/app/scope FAILS on Exchange rather than creating a second assignment — grants.rs:74-78 records exactly that ('every duplicate `New-RoleAssignment` failed'); (b) `remove_exchange_mailbox_access` (grants.rs:459-468) enumerates every assignment via `Get-ManagementRoleAssignment -RoleAssignee` and removes each, so even a duplicate would not leave access behind; (c) `assign_scoped_roles` (grants.rs:92-93) plans against the live snapshot, so a replay-induced 'failed to assign' leaves `role_in_place = false` and `targets_safe_to_strip` keeps the org-wide grant — fail-closed, healed on re-run; (d) `ensure_management_scope`/`ensure_service_principal` re-read before creating, and `Add-DistributionGroupMember` already treats 'already a member' as success (error.rs:166, tests.rs:412). So the realistic consequence is a misreported outcome (a committed write replayed surfaces as 'failed to assign' / 'failed to remove') and a wasted re-run, not widened or persisting access. Medium, not high.
verdicts.corrected_title: Exchange transport open-codes the retry loop with no RetryClass, so New-/Remove- cmdlets are replayed after transient failures and misreport a committed write as a failure; the hand-rolled loop escapes the trust.rs invariant
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Port `send_core` onto `with_retries(label, class, |_| ...)` with a `retry_class_for(cmdlet)` helper: `Get-`/`Test-`/`Search-` and paging continuations → Idempotent; `New-`/`Remove-`/`Set-`/`Update-` → NonIdempotent (`Add-DistributionGroupMember` may stay Idempotent since `is_already_member_body` already makes a re-add benign). Keep the `x-ms-diagnostics`/`request-id` capture inside the per-attempt closure. Extend `repo_invariants/trust.rs` so any crate source outside `http_retry.rs` that references `MAX_RETRIES`, `next_backoff_ms` or `sleep_before_retry` directly (rather than via `with_retries`/`RetryBudget`) fails the test. Add a wiremock test that a `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` answered 502 is NOT re-sent and a `Get-*` answered 502 IS. Fix the http_retry.rs:160-165 doc that presents the four-client unification as complete. Drop the 'duplicate assignment survives removal' framing — grants.rs:74-78 and 459-468 show Exchange rejects the duplicate and removal sweeps every assignment.

verdicts.notes: Evidence is exact. `mutate` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:121-123) starts from `Self::stored`, which is `from_file(..).unwrap_or_default()` (75-77), and `from_file` (223-232) collapses both an I/O error (`std::fs::read(path).ok()?` — EACCES/EIO/AV lock) and a parse error into `None` with only a `warn!`. `save_locked` then serialises the defaults over the file. private_file.rs:39-41 documents this exact loss mechanism but only closed the torn-write cause; defaults.rs:125-126 explicitly anticipates hand-edited settings.json. `remember_account` (state.rs:345-355) runs `mutate` on every successful sign-in, so the overwrite happens promptly. No `.bak`/`.corrupt` sibling or recovery exists (grep). No test covers 'unparseable file survives a mutate'. One nuance on the proposal: only two of the four writer files treat a `mutate` error as non-fatal (state.rs:347-355 warn, keyvault.rs:167-171 push a warning); config.rs:52-57 and defaults.rs:72-75 return `UiError::io('Could not write settings.json: ...')` to the operator — which is the desirable behaviour for a refused write, so the proposal still fits. Medium is honest: silent, permanent loss of `app_vaults`/tenant defaults, but requires a prior corruption/read failure.

The mechanics are correct: `temp_sibling` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/private_file.rs:57-61) yields `<target>.tmp<pid>`, and `write_then_rename` (67-75) opens with `create(true).truncate(true)` and no `create_new`/`O_NOFOLLOW`, deliberately reusing a pre-existing temp (comment at 73-74); `set_permissions` is fchmod on the followed target, so a pre-planted symlink in the destination directory is followed, truncated, overwritten with the payload, and `rename(temp, path)` (85) moves the symlink into place. export.rs:103 (every operator-chosen export, .pfx via credentials.rs:200) is the exposed call site; `settings.json` lives in the per-user config dir and is not. No test covers a symlink temp. However the severity is overstated: it needs a unix host, a world-writable/shared directory the operator picks in a save dialog, the victim's pid, and a filename that carries a to-the-second timestamp (export.rs:56-59, 153; credentials.rs:195-199), which the attacker must pre-plant before the open; Windows — the primary target per README — needs symlink privilege. Disclosure additionally requires the attacker to hold a pre-opened fd on the victim file, since the fchmod leaves it 0600. A real but narrow hardening item; the fix is cheap and standard.
verdicts.corrected_title: private_file temp path is predictable and opened without O_EXCL, so a symlink pre-planted in a shared export directory is followed — cheap hardening with create_new
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Open the temp with `.create_new(true)` (O_CREAT|O_EXCL refuses to follow an existing symlink, so no libc/`O_NOFOLLOW` is needed — libc is not a direct dependency of core) and add an in-process `AtomicU64` counter to the temp name so a stale temp from a crashed run yields `AlreadyExists` once and is retried with the next suffix (or removed first). With `create_new`, the `set_permissions` call becomes belt-and-braces and its 'reused temp' comment at 73-74 should be rewritten. Add a unix-only test that a pre-existing `<name>.tmp<pid>` symlink to a decoy file causes the write to fail (or use a fresh name) and leaves the decoy untouched.

verdicts.notes: Verified at crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs: lines 90-97 ('Writes the settings ... Used by the first-run config screen — the only writer of this file. Owner-only: ...') run straight into line 98 ('Read, modify and write ... under a process-wide lock') as one doc block on `mutate`, while `save` at 136-141 is `pub`, undocumented, not under `SETTINGS_LOCK`, and byte-identical to the private `save_locked` (129-134) whose doc says it is private 'so a caller cannot take the read-modify-write apart'. Production callers of `.save(` outside settings.rs: none (config.rs:52, defaults.rs:72, keyvault.rs:167, state.rs:347/363 all use `mutate`); only tests at 281 and 322 use it. No repo_invariants test mentions `UserSettings`/`mutate` (grep). The finding is real and the proposal is right, but with zero production callers and every call site carrying a 'through mutate, not stored + save' comment, this is a cleanup rather than a live race — low, not medium.

All three statements check out. crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:1-2 says 'the four typed clients share' while its own body (4-8) and the macro users (graph/error.rs:10, arm/error.rs:10, keyvault/error.rs:10) show three; http_error.rs:23 says 'nine common variants' but the macro emits ten (Unauthorized, Forbidden, NotFound, Throttled, Api, Server, Network, Deserialize, Token, Protocol at 73-101). http_retry.rs:160-165 ('The four HTTP clients each open-coded this loop', past tense) is contradicted by exchange transport.rs:181-188/265-270 still doing so. `ExchangeError::Forbidden { detail, had_diagnostics }` (exchange/src/error.rs:12-21) genuinely cannot be expressed by the macro's `extra` arm, so Exchange staying hand-written is defensible — but nothing in docs/architecture or AGENTS.md records that exception (grep `had_diagnostics` in docs: none), and Exchange has no `error_conformance.rs` unlike arm/keyvault. Note `.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:19` already correctly says 'Graph/ARM/Key Vault'. Option (b) — fix both docs and name the exception — is proportionate; option (a) is more machinery than the drift warrants unless done alongside the Exchange retry port ([1]).

Each cited drift is real. constants.rs:58-61 says the per-object cap applies to 'currently only ServicePrincipal', but `Cache::cap_for` (cache.rs:601-603) applies it to `ServicePrincipal | Lists`, and `capacity_for`'s doc (cache.rs:575-587) already lists both kinds — so constants.rs contradicts cache.rs. cache.rs:4-5 ('Eviction is LRU once per-kind entry count exceeds MAX_CACHE_SIZE') and constants.rs:47-48 ('5000-entry-per-kind cap') ignore `MAX_PER_OBJECT_CACHE_SIZE`. AGENTS.md:110 says 'two writers read-modify-write via `UserSettings::stored`'; actual writers are `mutate` call sites in config.rs:52, defaults.rs:72, keyvault.rs:167, state.rs:347/363 (four files, five sites), and settings.rs:100-103 itself says 'three'. The same stale sentence also lives in `.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:26` ('Two writers ... via `UserSettings::stored`'), which the reviewer did not cite and which should be fixed together with AGENTS.md. Low is right: doc-only, but AGENTS.md is loaded every session.
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Update constants.rs:58-61 to name both `ServicePrincipal` and `Lists` and point at `Cache::cap_for`/`capacity_for`; reword cache.rs:4-5 and constants.rs:47-48 to say the cap is `MAX_CACHE_SIZE` for aggregate kinds and `MAX_PER_OBJECT_CACHE_SIZE` for the two per-object kinds. Change AGENTS.md:110 AND `.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:26` to 'every writer (config, tenant defaults, vault binding, remembered account) goes through `UserSettings::mutate`', and align settings.rs:100 ('three') with the same count.

verdicts.notes: Verified at crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/defaults.rs:117-131, 139-153, 159-173: three bodies identical except for the field and prefix, each carrying the same 8-line comment; commands/defaults.rs:53-57 already iterates the three patterns as a table. Tests (defaults.rs:182-206 and below) exercise all three, so a shared `resolve_pattern` is a safe refactor. One overstatement: the comment on `secret_name_for` is not strictly irrelevant — it ends with 'the same collapse cross-wires Key Vault secret names between apps' — it is a copy-pasted shared rationale rather than a misattribution. Low/refactor is the honest severity; the placeholder guard is the load-bearing part and centralising it is worthwhile.

cache.rs:608-619 shows `clear` bumping all watches (`bump_watches(None, |_| true)`) and `clear_kind` bumping only its kind (`Some(kind)`); `bump_watches` (1037-1044) filters on `k.idx() == *watched_kind`, so the two behaviours the reviewer wants asserted are exactly what the code does today. `grep clear crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/cache/tests.rs` returns nothing; the watch tests (tests.rs:68-135 and onwards) cover `invalidate_prefix`/`invalidate`/`invalidate_tenant` only, and no src-tauri test drives `clear_cache` (diagnostics.rs:33-46). Both proposed tests are ~10 lines using `generation_for` + `put_typed_index_if_current`, consistent with the existing style. Low is right.

cache.rs:37-42 hand-lists `ALL: [CacheKind; 4]`, `idx()` (45-47) is `self as usize`, and `buckets: [Mutex<Bucket>; CacheKind::ALL.len()]` (366). The comment at 31-36 correctly notes `ttl_for` forces a new variant to be handled there (and `record` at 1108-1120 does too), but nothing forces `ALL` to grow: a fifth variant compiles and `buckets[4]` panics on first `get`/`put`. No test asserts `ALL[i].idx() == i` (grep). The proposal — exhaustive `match` in `idx()`, a `const` assert tying `ALL.len()` to the last discriminant + 1, and a small unit test — is cheap and idiomatic; collapsing `CacheStats` into `[Counters; ALL.len()]` is optional and would change the DTO shape diagnostics reads, so keep it separate. Low: latent, only bites on a future variant, but the failure mode is a runtime panic inside a Tauri command.

settings.rs:116-120 shows a process-wide `static Mutex`, so two processes can interleave `stored()`/`save_locked()`. No single-instance plugin is registered (lib.rs:24-25 has only updater + dialog; grep for `single_instance`/`File::lock`/`fs2`/`fd-lock` finds nothing), so a second instance is possible on Windows (the primary target) and Linux. rust-toolchain.toml:5 pins 1.98.1, above the 1.89 stabilisation of `File::lock`/`try_lock`/`unlock`, so an advisory lock on `<config_dir>/settings.lock` needs no new dependency and composes with the atomic rename in private_file. The race requires two instances writing within milliseconds of each other, which is rare in practice — low/enhancement is honest. Note `File::lock` releases when the `File` is dropped (or `unlock()`), so holding the `File` for the read-modify-write scope is sufficient; keep it inside the existing `SETTINGS_LOCK` so in-process callers still serialise without contending on the OS lock.

result.area_summary: Toolchain health is strong: all 591 library-crate tests and all 200 web-rs host tests pass (0 failures; 2 deliberately `ignore`d doctests), default-level clippy is clean on the libraries, the wasm `cargo check --all-targets --features test-support` is clean, all 10 packages share rust-version 1.98 / edition 2024 via `workspace = true`, and every member carries `[lints] workspace = true` (web-rs restates it and `repo_invariants/release.rs:24-40` pins the two blocks together). Duplicate majors are all explained and none is unifiable by a local bump: root = RustCrypto 0.10 stack (p12-keystore 0.2.1, the documented hold) vs 0.11 stack (secret-service 5.2.0 via zbus-secret-service-keyring-store 1.0.1), rand 0.8/rand_core 0.6/getrandom 0.2 (oauth2 5.0.0 + ring 0.17), and the GTK3/Tauri upstream set (bitflags 1, thiserror 1, syn 1, toml_edit 0.19/0.20, proc-macro-crate 1/2, indexmap 1 + hashbrown 0.12 via schemars 0.8, miniz_oxide 0.8 via png 0.17); web = base64 0.22 (leptos_server/server_fn, documented in web-rs Cargo.toml), reactive_stores 0.2.5 + dashmap 6 + hashbrown 0.14 (thaw_utils 0.2.0-beta, and thaw 0.5.0-beta is the latest release), convert_case 0.6/0.8/0.11 (leptos_config/reactive_stores_macro/leptos_macro), thiserror 1 (gloo-net 0.6 via server_fn). The weak spots are gates that don't exist rather than gates that fail: there is no unused-dependency check (six confirmed unused deps across five manifests), CI runs only clippy's default lint set (a pedantic pass finds 99 redundant clones in the wasm bundle and one blocking keyring call on the tokio worker), and graph/exchange lack the error-conformance pins that arm/keyvault have.

findings.title: Blocking keyring delete runs inline on the tokio worker (and under the refresh lock), contradicting the crate's own rule
findings.rationale: save_refresh_token (:457) and load_refresh_token (:509) are both wrapped in tokio::task::spawn_blocking with an explicit comment saying why, but delete_refresh_token is called synchronously twice: at :535 inside the refresh path while the refresh mutex is held (exactly the scenario the :503-506 comment warns about), and at :564 in sign_out. delete_chunks performs one OS keyring round trip per chunk (Windows Credential Manager; Linux secret-service over D-Bus via zbus), so an invalid-grant purge or a sign-out stalls the async worker and every other tokio task for the duration. The clippy `unused_async` hit on sign_out is the symptom that led here.
findings.proposal: Wrap both calls the same way as save/load: `let (t, oid) = (tenant.tenant_id.clone(), tenant.account_oid.clone()); tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || delete_refresh_token(&t, &oid)).await.map_err(|e| AuthError::Keyring(format!("keyring delete task failed: {e}")))??;` at :564, and the `let _ =` form of the same at :535. Consider a private `async fn delete_refresh_token_blocking(&self, tenant)` helper so a third caller cannot regress. Effect: no tokio worker stall during sign-out or refresh-token purge; sign_out's `async` becomes genuine and the lint goes away.

findings.title: http_error_enum! hard-codes `::thiserror::Error`, forcing every consumer crate to declare thiserror it never otherwise uses
findings.rationale: Because the macro resolves `::thiserror` in the consumer's namespace, arm/graph/keyvault must each carry a dependency they never name in source. That makes cargo-machete (and any future reader) report three false positives, and a crate that adopts the macro later will fail to compile with a confusing "unresolved crate thiserror" error until it copies the dep. The standard fix is the `$crate` re-export idiom.

Effect: consumers need only `azapptoolkit-core`; the macro's contract is self-contained; machete runs clean without ignore metadata.

findings.title: graph and exchange lack the error-conformance tests that arm and keyvault have; arm's header misdescribes graph's coverage
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md's "One definition per policy" rule is pinned by four tests in arm and keyvault (retryable set is exactly throttle/server/network; Token keeps its re-auth-fatal code; 403 hint comes from the capabilities catalog). Graph, the highest-volume client, has none of them, and exchange — the ONE client whose ui_code is hand-rolled rather than macro-generated (its Forbidden is a struct variant the macro cannot express) — is precisely "the part a hand-rolled re-implementation would get subtly wrong" that arm's own test header says is worth pinning. If someone flattens ExchangeError::Token to "token_error", every Exchange fan-out would again warn its way through a dead session, and no test would notice. The arm header's claim that graph has "a dedicated tests/ tree" is also false (graph's tests are in-crate under src/client/tests/), which is how the gap went unnoticed.
findings.proposal: Add crates/azapptoolkit-graph/tests/error_conformance.rs and crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/tests/error_conformance.rs mirroring arm's four tests (every_variant(), retryable set == [throttled, server_error, network_error], REAUTH_FATAL_CODES survive Token(...) and are not retryable, Forbidden hint == capability("exchange_rbac").remediation for had_diagnostics: true and Some(_) for false).     where
        B: Serialize + ?Sized,
clippy (nursery, 8 sites): warning: future cannot be sent between threads safely — "has type `&B` which is not `Send`, because `B` is not `Sync`" at transport.rs:92, :111, :126, :397, :417; applications.rs:587 (patch_application_web); service_principals.rs:618 (patch_service_principal); keyvault/src/client.rs:118 (send_json).
findings.rationale: Tauri `#[tauri::command] async fn`s must return Send futures, so today every call compiles only because each concrete body type happens to be Sync. A future caller passing a body holding a `Cell`/`Rc`/`RefCell` (or a `dyn Serialize` without `+ Sync`) would fail deep inside `generate_handler!` with an opaque "future is not Send" error rather than at the helper. All eight warnings share this single root cause.
findings.proposal: Add `+ Sync` to the `B` bound on the eight generic helpers (`B: Serialize + ?Sized + Sync`). No call site changes (all current bodies are Sync). Effect: Send-ness becomes a signature-level guarantee; the eight nursery warnings disappear, which also makes `future_not_send` enableable on the libraries if desired.

verdicts.corrected_proposal: Reimplement `scoped_send_core` on `send_core_url_with(token, retry_class_for(&method), method, url, &[], false, body_value, None)` — derive the class from the verb (as `send_core_url` does at transport.rs:449-461 and as the `repo_invariants/trust.rs:135` invariant expects) rather than hardcoding `RetryClass::NonIdempotent`, so scoped DELETEs (`remove_site_permission`, `remove_list_permission`, `remove_group_member`, claims-policy unassign) stay idempotent-replayable while POST/PATCH are replayed only after a 429. Update the doc comments at transport.rs:78-82 and the sharepoint/policies callers' expectations; keep `scoped_get` one-shot (pinned by tests/transport.rs:306). Add the two wiremock tests as proposed (429 Retry-After:0 then 201 succeeds; 502 on a scoped POST hits `.expect(1)`).
verdicts.notes: Premise verified. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/transport.rs:120-155 `scoped_send_core` does a single `req.send()` and maps the status with `map_error_status`; the rationale at :78-82 ('one-shot configuration writes, not high-volume reads') predates the loops that now call it: `add_group_member` (directory.rs:216-224) is invoked per restored SP in commands/restore.rs:709-716; `grant_list_permission`/`grant_list_item_permission` (sharepoint.rs:475-516, both `scoped_send_json`) run inside the dedupe_targets loop at commands/sharepoint.rs:566-600 (added in cf32c3d, 2026-08-28). core/http_retry.rs:113-114 documents `Throttled` as safe to replay for any verb, and `send_core_url_with` already takes an explicit provider + class (transport.rs:472-482). The only test pinning one-shot behaviour is for the scoped GET (`list_synchronization_jobs`, tests/transport.rs:306-333), not the write family, so no pinned decision is contradicted. Rides the AGENTS.md 'one definition per policy' rule: these writes bypass `core::http_retry` entirely and never notify the throttle observer. One refinement to the proposal: hardcoding NonIdempotent would downgrade the scoped DELETEs that today would be Idempotent under `retry_class_for`.

Premise verified by enumerating callers. transport.rs:175-181 `collect_all_pages` hardcodes `collect_all_pages_with(page, true)`. Of its 12 callers, only directory.rs:174 (`list_service_principal_groups`) and service_principals.rs:149 (`list_tenant_app_role_resources`) issue page 1 with `true`; the other ten (applications.rs:387 owners, :573 templates via `get_json_prefer` which passes `false`, batch.rs:172 `finish_paged_batch`, credentials.rs:82 federated creds, roles_grants.rs:62/:85/:182/:202, service_principals.rs:118/:406) issue page 1 with `false` and then page with `eventual`. The SP index inverts it: service_principals.rs:168-183 sends `$count=true` + `eventual` on page 1 and `collect_all_pages_capped(page, SP_INDEX_MAX, false)` at :203-205; its stated reason (:161-164, 'keeps the response shape identical to the prior index calls') is not functional, and `total_count` is dropped (the fn returns `Vec<ServicePrincipal>`). Microsoft's paging doc (learn.microsoft.com/graph/paging, point 5; graph/query-parameters#skiptoken) states the ConsistencyLevel header 'isn't included by default in subsequent page requests. It must be set explicitly' for advanced queries — so the SP index's `false` continuation is the clearly wrong half, while the ten `false→true` sites read pages 2+ from the eventually-consistent index store, which can miss a just-written grant on a security-posture read. No test asserts the page-2 header: tests/applications.rs:365-405 `list_applications_all_follows_next_link` has no header matcher, and `header_is_missing("consistencylevel")` appears only on page-1 mocks (:37, :63). The transport's own history (transport.rs:307-316) shows this exact drift produced a silent wrong answer once. Proposal (drop the defaulted wrapper, pass the page-1 flag at every site) is mechanical and matches applications.rs:219-228's single-predicate rule.

verdicts.corrected_title: Inner $batch 5xx sub-responses are terminal while the same GET alone is retried — one transient 503 sub-response marks the whole site sweep incomplete/uncached and strands a DR backup object
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Extend the re-batch predicate at batch.rs:281 to `matches!(sub.status, 429 | 502 | 503 | 504) && budget.may_retry()`, notifying the throttle observer for 429 only; `budget.wait(max_retry_after)` already falls back to jittered exponential backoff when no inner Retry-After exists (core/http_retry.rs:265-269), so no new backoff code is needed. Add a wiremock test mirroring `batch_get_json_retries_inner_429_then_surfaces_throttled` with an inner 503 that succeeds on the second POST, and one where an inner 503 that exhausts the budget still surfaces as `Server`.
verdicts.notes: Core premise verified: batch.rs:279-289 re-batches only `sub.status == 429`; :72-74 maps 5xx straight to `GraphError::Server`; the single-request path retries every non-4xx (transport.rs:612-621 `_ => None` → `Attempt::Retry`). Two parts are overstated or stale: (1) the cited Microsoft guidance (learn.microsoft.com/graph/throttling#throttling-and-batching) says to retry each *throttled* (429) request from a batch individually — it does not speak to 5xx sub-responses; (2) the 'audit prewarm cold lean-SP entry' example is stale — the batched lean prewarm was replaced by the SP index scan (commands/audit.rs:190-199). The real consumers are the DR backup, where a `Server` sub-error becomes a recorded `SkippedObject` (commands/backup.rs:397-441, 811) — honest, but a re-run is needed — and, unmentioned by the reviewer, the site sweep, where `batch_list_site_permissions` (sharepoint.rs:45-63) sub-errors are folded into `sites_failed`, which makes the whole 5000-site sweep incomplete and uncached (commands/sharepoint.rs:975-992). Enhancement, not a correctness bug, since both paths degrade honestly; medium is defensible because of the sweep cost.

verdicts.corrected_title: remove_key_credential / remove_service_principal_key_credential PATCH the unchanged array and report success when the key id is absent — and the remediation counts it as a removal
verdicts.corrected_proposal: In both removers, detect an empty match (compare lengths, or `find` the entry first) and return `Err(GraphError::NotFound(format!("keyCredential {key_id}")))` without sending the PATCH. Then adjust the callers, because none of them currently handles NotFound as 'already gone': `remediate_remove_expired_credentials` (commands/remediation.rs:69-79) should treat NotFound from either `remove_password` or `remove_key_credential` as already-removed (skip, do not increment `removed_*`, do not abort the loop) rather than surfacing it as a failure; `remove_certificate_credential` (commands/applications/credentials.rs:236-247) and the SSO retire path (commands/sso/mod.rs:960-963) can let NotFound propagate. Add the wiremock test asserting no PATCH is sent for an unknown key id.
verdicts.notes: Premise verified: credentials.rs:198-209 filters `live_key_credentials` by `keyId` and PATCHes whatever remains, returning `Ok(())` even when nothing matched; credentials.rs:251-300 (`remove_service_principal_key_credential`) has the same shape (with a `thumbprint` of `None` the filter is a no-op and the PATCH is still sent). The remediation at commands/remediation.rs:77-82 then increments `removed_certificates` and busts caches via `invalidate_app_credentials` (:91-93). What is overstated: the reviewer says 'Callers already map NotFound for the password path' — they do not; remediation.rs:69-73 breaks and returns the error on any `remove_password` failure, and there is no 'already gone' handling anywhere on these paths (grep for NotFound/already in remediation.rs and applications/credentials.rs returns nothing). So the proposal as written would turn a concurrently-removed certificate from a silently-counted success into a hard remediation failure; the caller change above is needed for the fix to be an improvement. The `remove_password` 404 claim is plausible (Graph's `removePassword` action rejects an unknown keyId) but is not something the repo pins. Low is right.

The 'automatically' claim is the kind that leads to the silent `$count`-ignored failure Microsoft documents. Doc-only, low; proposed wording is accurate.

Traced end to end; nothing upstream gates the check. (1) apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/updater.rs:26-28 `check_for_update` and :44-46 `perform_update` call `app.updater()?.check().await` unconditionally; no settings read anywhere in the file. (2) `UserSettings::load` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:83-89, the only place `auto_update_env_override` at :235 is applied) has zero callers outside that module's own tests — every production reader uses `UserSettings::stored` (state.rs:234, :376; commands/exchange/mod.rs:74; commands/defaults.rs:19) or `mutate`. `grep auto_update` under apps/ returns nothing: the field is never read by the backend or web-rs, so neither the env var nor `{"auto_update": false}` in settings.json has any effect. (3) Reachable in the shipped build: tauri.conf.json:45-48 has `plugins.updater.active: true` with the GitHub `releases/latest/download/latest.json` endpoint, capabilities/default.json:10 grants `updater:default`, lib.rs:24 registers the plugin and lib.rs:43-44 exposes both commands. (4) The frontend fires the check on every mount with no policy check: web-rs/src/views/shell.rs:162-177 (`Effect::new` -> `updater::check_for_update()`), plus the manual path at :189 which toasts 'You're on the latest version.' on `Ok(None)`; no `auto_update` binding, view, or toggle exists in web-rs. (5) Docs promise the opposite: README.md:264-282 documents both opt-outs and states 'With auto-update disabled the app makes no network calls to the updater endpoint at any point in the session'; README.md:255-259 tells MSI deployers to rely on this to avoid a second conflicting NSIS install; docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:314 cites a 'settings toggle' that does not exist; docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md:42-50 never mentions the opt-out at all. Repo-invariant tests (tests/repo_invariants/release.rs) pin version/notes parity only, not the opt-out. Git history in this clone shows no src-tauri commit ever referencing `auto_update`, so this is not a recent regression — the gate was never wired. Mitigating factor that keeps this from being worse: installation still requires the user to click 'Update & restart' (UpdateSplash), so the failure is unexpected egress + a misleading update prompt (and the MSI-conflict guidance being ineffective), not a silent install. High stands because the README makes an explicit no-egress guarantee to MDM/CI operators and the MSI guidance depends on it.
verdicts.corrected_title: Documented auto-update opt-out (AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE / settings.json auto_update) is never consulted — check_for_update/perform_update and the shell launch check ignore it

Surface the policy to the frontend (e.g. fold `disabled_by_policy` into the check result or add an `update_policy` command with a `bindings/updater.rs` stub) so the account-menu 'Check for updates' item shows 'Update checks are disabled by policy' rather than 'You're on the latest version.' verdicts.corrected_title: Key Vault `retry_class_for` doc comment contradicts itself about `setSecret` (a PUT) — clarify the deliberate same-value replay rather than reclassify PUT
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Rewrite the doc comment at crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs:261-266 to state the actual trade-off: Key Vault `PUT /secrets/{name}` appends a version on every call, so a replay after an unknown outcome can produce a second version — but the replay carries the identical value, so the current version is always correct and the only cost is a duplicate same-value version. Optionally add a wiremock test (502 then 200) asserting both PUT bodies are byte-identical and the call succeeds. Do NOT route PUT to `NonIdempotent` for this crate: that would fail the rotation on a pre-commit transient 502 and, on a post-commit one, `rotate_app_credential` (commands/keyvault.rs:123-128) would remove the freshly minted app secret while the vault already holds it — a dead value in the vault is worse than a duplicate live one.

The premise — 'Reads against a Disabled/Deleted subscription fail' — is contradicted by Microsoft Learn 'Azure subscription states': Disabled, Warned, Expired and Past Due subscriptions all explicitly allow GET ('Your resources are still available, so you can retrieve or delete them (GET, DELETE)'; only PUT/PATCH/POST are blocked), and Deleted subscriptions have their resources removed and are not a persistent listing state. So the fan-outs in managed_identity.rs:223-246, keyvault_rbac.rs:113-131, keyvault.rs:204-227, readiness.rs:220-250 and usage.rs:90-115 do not pay failed round trips for non-Enabled subscriptions, and `skipped`/`vaults_failed` are not inflated by them. Worse, the proposal to partition out `state != "Enabled"` would HIDE genuine role assignments and vaults on disabled subscriptions — grants that become live again on reactivation — which is a regression for a security-posture tool. Adding `state` to `Subscription` (models.rs:14-20) as display metadata would be harmless but has no coverage-accuracy benefit.

Failing path traced end to end; nothing upstream prevents it.

1. The permissions are real Graph APPLICATION permissions (admin-consent, tenant-wide). Microsoft Graph permissions reference lists `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All` (id 1583d471-fede-4e7c-b062-57e9d60cfb49, Application), `MailboxFolder.ReadWrite.All` (fef87b92-...), `MailboxItem.Read.All`, `MailboxItem.Export.All`, `MailboxItem.ImportExport.All`, and `Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All` (e118f1da-5c1c-46cf-bff6-8858d786f46f, 'create, read, update, and delete all email ... in user mailboxes, without a signed-in user'). The RBAC-for-Applications doc's 'Supported Application Roles' table (fetched live) maps each to an `Application MailboxItem.*` / `Application MailboxFolder.*` / `Application Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All` role, protocol MS Graph.

2. Advisory membership: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/scoping.rs:204 `Some(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID) => graph_mail_role(value).is_some() || mailbox_named(value)`. `graph_mail_role` (scoping.rs:77-92) has no arm for any of these -> None. `mailbox_named` (scoping.rs:194-198) tests only `Mail.`, `MailboxSettings.`, `Calendars.`, `Contacts.`; `"MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All".starts_with("MailboxSettings.")` is false and `"Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All".starts_with("Mail.")` is false (char 5 is '-' not '.'). So `is_mailbox_reaching_permission(Some(GRAPH), v)` is false, and the filter at audit/scoring.rs:288-296 drops the grant before the scoped/org-wide/unconfinable partition; neither ORG_WIDE_MAILBOX, UNSCOPABLE_LEGACY_MAILBOX nor UNCONFINABLE_MAILBOX (scoring.rs:350-361) is emitted and no ScopeMailboxAccess fix is offered. The fallback's own comment (scoping.rs:200-203) says it exists precisely so 'a Graph permission this build's graph_mail_role table doesn't know yet still reports reach', which is exactly what fails here.

3. Scoring: rule_app_permission_risk (scoring.rs:49-92) is exact-match `HIGH_RISK_APP_PERMISSIONS.contains(&g.value.as_str())` / MEDIUM; neither table (audit/permissions.rs:67-140) has any MailboxItem/MailboxFolder/Mail-Advanced entry (grep across all *.rs: zero hits outside docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md:46-47). No generic `.All` / `ReadWrite` heuristic exists anywhere in audit (grep for ends_with(".All")/contains("ReadWrite") finds only tests). rule_admin_consent (scoring.rs:201-213) fires on `has_admin_consent`, i.e. DELEGATED consent, not app-role grants. `least_privilege_alternative_for` (permissions.rs:264-277) routes through `is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission` -> None. The bundled permissions catalog (azapptoolkit-permissions/data/catalog.json) holds only `appId`/`displayName` per resource — no permission values — so it cannot supply a fallback. The only test guarding the mailbox-family/risk-table agreement (permissions.rs:603-605) also uses `Mail.`/`Calendar`/`Contacts.` prefixes and so cannot notice the gap. No repo_invariants test references mailbox_named or these names.

Net: an app holding only Graph `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All` or `Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All` contributes 0 points and zero mailbox issues -> healthy row in a security audit whose purpose is to surface exactly this. Reachable in the shipped build (core scoring, not test/demo code). Severity high stands: silent false negative on tenant-wide mailbox content read/write/export. The doc's deliberate exclusion (exchange-scoping.md:46-49) concerns the scopable set / AAP parity, not advisory membership, so it does not justify the omission.
verdicts.corrected_proposal: (1) Extend `mailbox_named` in scoping.rs:194-198 with "MailboxFolder.", "MailboxItem.", "MailboxConfigItem.", "Mail-Advanced." (and consider "MailTips." only if the team wants metadata-only reach in the advisory), plus a table test iterating Microsoft's supported-roles list asserting `is_mailbox_reaching_permission(Some(GRAPH), v)` for every Graph row. Because these will then land in `unconfinable_other`, either (a) add them to `graph_mail_role` (scoping.rs:77-92) with the CHANGELOG note exchange-scoping.md:46-49 requires, so they get ORG_WIDE_MAILBOX + the ScopeMailboxAccess fix, or (b) reword the UNCONFINABLE_MAILBOX recommendation at scoring.rs:355-360, which currently asserts 'RBAC for Applications exposes no supported application role for them' — false for this family. (2) Add `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All`, `MailboxItem.Export.All`, `MailboxItem.ImportExport.All`, `MailboxFolder.ReadWrite.All`, `Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All` to HIGH_RISK_APP_PERMISSIONS and `MailboxItem.Read.All`, `MailboxFolder.Read.All` to MEDIUM_RISK_APP_PERMISSIONS (tenant-wide write = high, read = medium, matching the tables' existing split), and widen the `mailbox_family` closure in the permissions.rs:603 agreement test so the two spellings stay in sync. Also update exchange-scoping.md:46-49 to say the roles are excluded from the *scopable* map only, not from advisory membership.

(1) Entry: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/config.rs:41-46,71-73 — `set_auth_config` accepts any dotted whitespace-free string via `is_valid_tenant` and persists it to settings.json; the frontend advertises it (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/config_screen.rs:125 placeholder "GUID or contoso.onmicrosoft.com", :176-177 "must be a GUID or a domain like contoso.onmicrosoft.com"). (2) No normalization anywhere: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/state.rs:128-146 `resolve` returns the raw string; state.rs:241-258 passes it verbatim to `EntraAuthService::new`, which stores it unchanged (crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:83-87). `grep openid-configuration` across the repo finds no discovery fetch; the only hit is commands/sso/mod.rs:100-104 `oidc_summary_urls`, a static string formatter for the SSO summary panel, not a lookup (so the proposal's "repo already does this discovery" is inaccurate, though the fix direction stands). (3) The authority `{auth_root}/contoso.onmicrosoft.com` (service/mod.rs:219) is valid for Entra, so /authorize + /token succeed and the id_token `tid` claim is the tenant GUID (Entra always emits tid as a GUID). service/mod.rs:313-318 then does an exact `tenant_id != self.tenant_id` string compare with no non-GUID branch and returns `AuthError::TokenExchange`, which the sign-in view maps to the generic `token_exchange` hint (sign_in.rs:164) that misleads the operator toward the client/tenant IDs. (4) Launch restore is independently blocked: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:162-166 `remembered_account_for` filters `account.tenant_id == tenant_id` (GUID from claims vs configured domain), called from state.rs:377. (5) No repo_invariants test or auth unit test covers a domain-form tenant (the only `tid` mismatch string exists at service/mod.rs:315; no test asserts it), and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:52,72 and README.md:401 document only GUIDs — the domain path was added to the config screen without ever being wired through. Severity stays high: an advertised, validated configuration path is 100% unusable end to end and the resulting error hint points at the wrong cause; only the GUID path works. Not a security exposure (the check fails closed), purely a correctness/UX bug.
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Either (a) drop domain support: make `is_valid_tenant` GUID-only and change the config_screen.rs placeholder/error text (lines 125, 176-177) and the config.rs:44 message to match; or (b) resolve a non-GUID tenant once to its GUID before constructing `EntraAuthService` (fetch `{auth_root}/{tenant}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration` and take the GUID from `issuer`, or accept the `tid` in `sign_in` when the configured value is not a GUID and then adopt the resolved GUID for `known_tenants`, the keyring key and `remembered_account_for`). Note commands/sso/mod.rs:100-104 only formats the discovery URL as a string — there is no existing discovery client to reuse. Add a `sign_in` test against a mock token endpoint (auth_root is already a field for that purpose, service/mod.rs:62-65) with a domain-configured service and a GUID `tid`, plus a settings.rs test that a domain-configured install restores its remembered account.

verdicts.notes: Failing path traced end to end and nothing upstream prevents it. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/sharepoint.rs:74-107: `list_all_sites` pages `/sites?search=*&$top=200` while `out.len() < max`; on a tenant with >5000 enumerable sites page 25 brings `out.len()` to exactly 5000, the `while` condition fails, `page.next_link` (still `Some`) is dropped, `out.truncate(max)` is a no-op and a bare `Vec` of 5000 is returned with no signal. The only other exit that guards paging (`pages >= MAX_PAGES` at :96) is a hard error, not a truncation, and at 200/page it sits at 40 000 sites, so the item cap is the sole silent-truncation path. Caller apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sharepoint.rs:842-846 binds `sites`, sets `total = sites.len()` (=5000), and :977-992 builds `SiteSweepResult { total_sites: total, sites_failed, cancelled }` and caches it under `CacheKind::Audit` when `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0` — neither field is affected by the cap, so the truncated sweep IS cached for the 60-min audit TTL. `get_cached_site_sweep` (:1005) and `get_app_site_access` (:1043) then serve it; both are in `generate_handler![]` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:208-211), so this is the shipped build, not tests/demo. crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sharepoint.rs:130 `is_complete()` = `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0` returns true, and apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/app_site_access_panel.rs:242-252 renders the affirmative empty state 'No per-site grants. This app reaches no site through the Sites.Selected model' when `complete`. The Sites tab summary (views/resource_access/sites.rs:112-135) prints 'scanned 5000 of 5000 sites' with no partial-coverage suffix. Grep of web-rs for 5000/5_000/MAX_SITES finds only the toast timeout — no frontend cap detection; `IndexCapNotice` (components/index_cap_notice.rs:47-80) is hard-wired to `sp_index_truncated` and never fires for the site sweep. The invariant this breaks is stated in docs/architecture/resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:30-34,49 ('Coverage is never overstated', 'no per-site grants is only claimed when every enumerable site was actually read') and in the command's own comment at commands/sharepoint.rs:757 ('Raise if a user legitimately hits it' — but nothing detects hitting it). The existing wiremock test (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/tests/sharepoint.rs:183-185) asserts only `capped.len() == 1` and cannot observe the dropped signal. Precondition is a tenant with >5000 team/communication sites, which is a large but realistic enterprise (Teams provisions one site per team); given the surface is a security-posture view that affirmatively asserts an app has no reach, high stands.
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Return `Result<(Vec<Site>, bool)>` from `list_all_sites`, computing the flag after the loop as `out.len() > max || page.next_link.is_some()` (the `MAX_PAGES` branch already hard-errors, so it needs no truncation flag — unlike `collect_all_pages_capped`). In `sweep_site_permissions` bind the flag, add an additive `truncated: bool` to `SiteSweepResult` and `AppSiteAccessDto` (copied in `from_sweep`), fold it into `is_complete()` (`!cancelled && sites_failed == 0 && !truncated`) and into the cache guard (`if !cancelled && sites_failed == 0 && !truncated`). On the frontend, `IndexCapNotice` cannot be reused as-is — it is keyed to `get_directory_index_status().sp_index_truncated`, not the sweep — so either append a truncation clause to the two summary strings (`views/resource_access/sites.rs` summary Memo and `app_site_access_panel::coverage_summary`) or render a `Callout tone="warn"` from `access.truncated` alongside them. Update the fixture at web-rs/src/ipc_mock/fixtures.rs:825 and the DTO tests; add a wiremock case in client/tests/sharepoint.rs where page 1 has a nextLink and `max` is already met, asserting `truncated == true`, plus one where the chain ends within the cap asserting `false`.
